paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.

paragraphs.sourceText: Scientists scanning and mapping the Giza pyramids say they’ve discovered that Great Pyramid of Giza is not exactly even. But really not by much. This pyramid is the oldest of the world’s Seven Wonders. The pyramid’s exact size has 26 experts for centuries, as the “more than 21 acres of hard, white casing stones “that originally covered it were 27 long ago. Reporting in the most recent issue of the newsletter “AERAGRAM,” which 28 the work or the Ancient Egypt Research Associates, engineer Glen Dash says his team used a new measuring approach that involved finding any surviving 29 , of the casing in order to determine where the original edge was. They found the east side of the pyramid to be a 30 of 5.5 inches shorter than the west side.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对吉萨金字塔进行扫描和测绘的科学家表示，他们发现吉萨大金字塔并不完全平坦。但确实相差不大。这座金字塔是世界七大奇迹中最古老的。几个世纪以来，金字塔的确切尺寸一直困扰着专家们，因为最初覆盖金字塔的“超过 21 英亩的坚硬白色外壳石”很久以前就被拆除了。工程师格伦·达什（Glen Dash）在最新一期的时事通讯“AERAGRAM”中报道了古埃及研究协会的这项工作，他说，他的团队使用了一种新的测量方法，包括寻找任何幸存的套管残余物，以确定原始边缘的位置。他们发现金字塔的东边比西边最多短 5.5 英寸。

paragraphs.sourceText: The question that most 31 him, however, isn’t how the Egyptians who designed and built the pyramid got it wrong 4,500 years age, but how they got it so close to 32 . “We can only speculate as to how the Egyptians could have laid out these lines with such 33 using only the tools they had,” Dash writes. He says his 34 is that the Egyptians laid out their design on a grid, noting that the great pyramid is oriented only 35 away from the cardinal directions(its north-south axis runs 3 minutes 54 seconds west of due north, while its east-west axis runs 3 minutes 51 seconds north of due east)—an amount that’s “tiny, but similar,” archeologist Atlas Obscura points out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，最让他着迷的问题不是设计和建造金字塔的埃及人在 4500 年前是如何出错的，而是他们如何将金字塔做得如此接近完美。 “我们只能推测埃及人如何仅使用他们拥有的工具就能够如此精确地布置这些线条，”达什写道。他说，他的假设是埃及人将他们的设计放在网格上，并指出大金字塔的方向仅稍微偏离基本方向（其南北轴线在正北以西 3 分 54 秒处延伸，而其东西轴线在正东以北 3 分 51 秒处延伸）——考古学家阿特拉斯·奥布斯库拉 (Atlas Obscura) 指出，这个距离“虽小，但相似”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Peer Pressure Has a Positive Side
paragraphs.translationZh: 同侪压力有积极的一面

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Parents of teenagers often view their children‘s friends with something like suspicion. They worry that the adolescent peer group has the power to push its members into behavior that is foolish and even dangerous. Such wariness is well founded: statistics show, for example, that a teenage driver with a same-age passenger in the car is at higher risk of a fatal crash than an adolescent driving alone or with an adult.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：青少年的父母经常以怀疑的态度看待孩子的朋友。他们担心青少年同龄群体有能力迫使其成员做出愚蠢甚至危险的行为。这种谨慎是有根据的：例如，统计数据显示，车内有同龄乘客的青少年司机比单独驾驶或与成年人一起驾驶的青少年发生致命车祸的风险更高。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. In a 2005 study, psychologist Laurence Steinberg of Temple University and his co-author, psychologist Margo Gardner, then at Temple, divided 306 people into three age groups: young adolescents, with a mean age of 14; older adolescents, with a mean age of 19; and adults, aged 24 and older. Subjects played a computerized driving game in which the player must avoid crashing into a wall that materializes, without warning, on the roadway. Steinberg and Gardner randomly assigned some participants to play alone or with two same-age peers looking on.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 在 2005 年的一项研究中，坦普尔大学的心理学家劳伦斯·斯坦伯格 (Laurence Steinberg) 和他的合著者、当时在坦普尔大学的心理学家玛戈·加德纳 (Margo Gardner) 将 306 人分为三个年龄组：年轻青少年，平均年龄为 14 岁；年龄较大的青少年，平均年龄为 19 岁；以及 24 岁及以上的成年人。受试者玩了一个计算机化的驾驶游戏，在游戏中，玩家必须避免撞到在没有警告的情况下出现在道路上的墙壁。斯坦伯格和加德纳随机分配一些参与者单独玩耍或与两个同龄的同伴一起玩耍。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Older adolescents scored about 50 percent higher on an index of risky driving when their peers were in the room—and the driving of early adolescents was fully twice as reckless when other young teens were around. In contrast, adults behaved in similar ways regardless of whether they were on their own or observed by others. “The presence of peers makes adolescents and youth, but not adults, more likely to take risks,” Steinberg and Gardner concluded.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 当同龄人在房间里时，年龄较大的青少年的危险驾驶指数得分高出约 50%，而当其他青少年在场时，早期青少年的鲁莽驾驶行为整整是前者的两倍。相比之下，成年人无论是独自一人还是在他人的观察下，都会表现出相似的行为方式。斯坦伯格和加德纳总结道：“同龄人的存在使青少年（而不是成年人）更有可能冒险。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Yet in the years following the publication of this study, Steinberg began to believe that this interpretation did not capture the whole picture. As he and other researchers examined the question of why teens were more apt to take risks in the company of other teenagers, they came to suspect that a crowd‘s influence need not always be negative. Now some experts are proposing that we should take advantage of the teen brain’s keen sensitivity to the presence of friends and leverage it to improve education.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 然而，在这项研究发表后的几年里，斯坦伯格开始相信这种解释并没有涵盖全部情况。当他和其他研究人员研究为什么青少年更容易在其他青少年的陪伴下冒险的问题时，他们开始怀疑群体的影响不一定总是负面的。现在一些专家建议，我们应该利用青少年大脑对朋友存在的敏锐敏感性，并利用它来改善教育。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. In a 2011 study, Steinberg and his colleagues turned to functional MRI （磁共振）to investigate how the presence of peers affects the activity in the adolescent brain. They scanned the brains of 40 teens and adults who were playing a virtual driving game designed to test whether players would brake at a yellow light or speed on through the crossroad.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 在 2011 年的一项研究中，斯坦伯格和他的同事利用功能性 MRI 来研究同龄人的存在如何影响青少年大脑的活动。他们扫描了 40 名正在玩虚拟驾驶游戏的青少年和成年人的大脑，该游戏旨在测试玩家是否会在黄灯亮时刹车或加速通过十字路口。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. The brains of teenagers, but not adults, showed greater activity in two regions associated with rewards when they were being observed by same-age peers than when alone. In other words, rewards are more intense for teens when they are with peers, which motivates them to pursue higher-risk experiences that might bring a big payoff （such as the thrill of just making the light before it turns red）. But Steinberg suspected this tendency could also have its advantages. In his latest experiment, published online in August, Steinberg and his colleagues used a computerized version of a card game called the Iowa Gambling Task to investigate how the presence of peers affects the way young people gather and apply information.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 青少年（而非成年人）的大脑在被同龄同龄人观察时，与奖励相关的两个区域表现出比单独观察时更大的活动。换句话说，当青少年与同龄人在一起时，奖励会更加强烈，这会激励他们追求可能带来巨大回报的高风险体验（例如在红灯变红之前让灯变红的兴奋感）。但斯坦伯格怀疑这种趋势也可能有其优势。在八月在线发表的最新实验中，斯坦伯格和他的同事使用了一种名为爱荷华州赌博任务的纸牌游戏的计算机化版本来调查同龄人的存在如何影响年轻人收集和应用信息的方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. The results: Teens who played the Iowa Gambling Task under the eyes of fellow adolescents engaged in more exploratory behavior, learned faster from both positive and negative outcomes, and achieved better performance on the task than those who played in solitude. “What our study suggests is that teenagers learn more quickly and more effectively when their peers are present than when they‘re on their own,” Steinberg says. And this finding could have important implications for how we think about educating adolescents.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 结果：在其他青少年的注视下玩爱荷华州赌博任务的青少年会进行更多的探索行为，从积极和消极的结果中学习得更快，并且比那些独自玩的人在任务中取得更好的表现。 “我们的研究表明，青少年在有同伴在场时比独自一人时学习得更快、更有效，”斯坦伯格说。这一发现可能对我们如何看待青少年教育产生重要影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. Matthew D. Lieberman, a social cognitive neuroscientist at the University of California, Los Angeles, and author of the 2013 book Social: Why Our Brains Are Wired to Connect，suspects that the human brain is especially adept at learning socially salient information. He points to a classic 2004 study in which psychologists at Dartmouth College and Harvard University used functional MRI to track brain activity in 17 young men as they listened to descriptions of people while concentrating on either socially relevant cues （for example, trying to form an impression of a person based on the description）or more socially neutral information （such as noting the order of details in the description）.The descriptions were the same in each condition, but people could better remember these statements when given a social motivation.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. Matthew D. Lieberman 是加州大学洛杉矶分校的社会认知神经科学家，也是 2013 年《社交：为什么我们的大脑需要连接》一书的作者，他怀疑人类大脑特别擅长学习社交显着信息。他提到了 2004 年的一项经典研究，其中达特茅斯学院和哈佛大学的心理学家使用功能性 MRI 来跟踪 17 名年轻人的大脑活动，他们在听对人的描述时，同时专注于与社会相关的线索（例如，试图根据描述形成对一个人的印象）或更社会中立的信息（例如注意描述中细节的顺序）。每种情况下的描述都是相同的，但当人们在社交环境中听到这些描述时，他们可以更好地记住这些陈述。动机。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. The study also found that when subjects thought about and later recalled descriptions in terms of their informational content, regions associated with factual memory, such as the medial temporal lobe, became active. But thinking about or remembering descriptions in terms of their social meaning activated the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex—part of the brain‘s social network—even as traditional memory regions registered low levels of activity. More recently, as he reported in a 2012 review, Lieberman has discovered that this region may be part of a distinct network involved in socially motivated learning and memory. Such findings, he says, suggest that “this network can be called on to process and store the kind of information taught in school—potentially giving students access to a range of untapped mental powers.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 研究还发现，当受试者思考并随后回忆起有关信息内容的描述时，与事实记忆相关的区域（例如内侧颞叶）就会变得活跃。但是，即使传统记忆区域的活动水平较低，思考或记住描述的社会意义也会激活背内侧前额叶皮层（大脑社交网络的一部分）。最近，正如利伯曼在 2012 年的一篇评论中所报告的那样，他发现该区域可能是涉及社会动机学习和记忆的独特网络的一部分。他说，这些发现表明“这个网络可以用来处理和存储学校教授的信息——有可能让学生获得一系列尚未开发的智力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J. If humans are generally geared to recall details about one another, this pattern is probably even more powerful among teenagers who are very attentive to social details: who is in, who is out, who likes whom, who is mad at whom. Their penchant for social drama is not—or not only—a way of distracting themselves from their schoolwork or of driving adults crazy. It is actually a neurological（神经的）sensitivity, initiated by hormonal changes. Evolutionarily speaking, people in this age group are at a stage in which they can prepare to find a mate and start their own family while separating from parents and striking out on their own. To do this successfully, their brain prompts them to think and even obsess about others.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 如果人类普遍倾向于回忆彼此的细节，那么这种模式在非常关注社会细节的青少年中可能更为强大：谁在，谁在外，谁喜欢谁，谁对谁生气。他们对社交戏剧的偏爱并不是——或者不仅仅是——一种分散学业注意力或让成年人发疯的方式。它实际上是一种由荷尔蒙变化引发的神经敏感性。从进化的角度来说，这个年龄段的人正处于准备寻找伴侣、组建自己的家庭、同时与父母分离、独立创业的阶段。为了成功地做到这一点，他们的大脑会促使他们思考甚至痴迷于他人。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Yet our schools focus primarily on students as individual entities. What would happen if educators instead took advantage of the fact that teens are powerfully compelled to think in social terms? In Social, Lieberman lays out a number of ways to do so. History and English could be presented through the lens of the psychological drives of the people involved. One could therefore present Napoleon in terms of his desire to impress or Churchill in terms of his lonely melancholy. Less inherently interpersonal subjects, such as math, could acquire a social aspect through team problem solving and peer tutoring. Research shows that when we absorb information in order to teach it to someone else, we learn it more accurately and deeply, perhaps in part because we are engaging our social cognition.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 然而，我们的学校主要关注作为个体实体的学生。如果教育工作者利用青少年强烈地被迫从社会角度思考这一事实，会发生什么？在《社交》一书中，利伯曼提出了多种实现这一目标的方法。历史和英语可以通过相关人员的心理驱动力的镜头来呈现。因此，人们可以用他想要给人留下深刻印象的方式来表现拿破仑，也可以用他孤独忧郁的方式来表现丘吉尔。数学等本质上不太人际交往的科目可以通过团队解决问题和同伴辅导获得社交方面的知识。研究表明，当我们吸收信息以便将其传授给别人时，我们会更准确、更深入地学习它，部分原因可能是我们正在调动我们的社会认知。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. And although anxious parents may not welcome the notion, educators could turn adolescent recklessness to academic ends. “Risk taking in an educational context is a vital skill that enables progress and creativity,” wrote Sarah-Jayne Blakemore, a cognitive neuroscientist at University College London, in a review published last year. Yet, she noted, many young people are especially risk averse at school—afraid that one low test score or mediocre grade could cost them a spot at a selective university. We should assure such students that risk, and even peer pressure, can be a good thing—as long as it happens in the classroom and not the car.
paragraphs.translationZh: L：虽然焦虑的父母可能不欢迎这个想法，但教育工作者可以将青少年的鲁莽行为转化为学术目的。伦敦大学学院的认知神经科学家莎拉·杰恩·布莱克莫尔在去年发表的一篇评论中写道：“在教育背景下，承担风险是一项至关重要的技能，可以促进进步和创造力。”然而，她指出，许多年轻人在学校特别厌恶风险，担心考试成绩低或成绩平庸可能会让他们失去进入名牌大学的机会。我们应该向这些学生保证，风险，甚至同伴压力，都可能是一件好事——只要它发生在教室而不是车里。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It is thought probable that the human brain is particularly good at picking-up socially important information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 人们认为人类大脑可能特别擅长获取对社会重要的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. It can be concluded from experiment that the presence of peers increases risk-taking by adolescents and youth.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 从实验中可以得出结论，同龄人的存在增加了青少年的冒险行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Students should be told that risk-taking in the classroom can be something positive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 应该告诉学生，在课堂上冒险可以是积极的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. The urge of finding a mate and getting married accounts for adolescents’ greater attention to social interactions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 寻找伴侣和结婚的冲动导致青少年更加关注社交互动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. According to Steinberg, the presence of peers increases the speed and effectiveness of teenagers’ leaning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 斯坦伯格认为，同龄人的存在可以提高青少年学习的速度和效率。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Teenagers’ parents are often concerned about negative peer influence.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 青少年的父母常常担心同伴的负面影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Activating the brain’s social network involved in socially motivated learning and memory may allow students to tap unused mental powers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 激活大脑参与社会动机学习和记忆的社交网络可以让学生挖掘未使用的心智力量。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The presence of peer intensifies the feeling of rewards in teens’ brains.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43.同伴的存在会增强青少年大脑中的奖励感。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. When we absorb information for the purpose of imparting it to others, we do so with greater secretary and depth.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Ebro Delta, in Spain, famous as a battleground during the Spanish Civil War, is now the setting for a different contest, one that is pitting rice farmers against two enemies: the rice-eating giant apple snail, and rising sea levels. What happens here will have a bearing on the future of European rice production and the overall health of southern European wetlands.
paragraphs.translationZh: 西班牙的埃布罗三角洲在西班牙内战期间作为战场而闻名，现在却成为了一场不同的竞赛的场所，这场竞赛是稻农与两个敌人的较量：以稻米为食的巨型苹果螺和不断上升的海平面。这里发生的事情将对欧洲水稻生产的未来和南欧湿地的整体健康产生影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: Located on the Mediterranean just two hours south of Barcelona, the Ebro Delta produces 120 million kilograms of rice a year, making it one of the continent’s most important rice-growing areas. As the sea creeps into these freshwater marshes, however, rising salinity （盐分）is hampering rice production. At the same time, this sea-water also kills off the greedy giant apple snail, an introduced pest that feeds on young rice plants. The most promising strategy has become to harness one foe against the other.
paragraphs.translationZh: 埃布罗三角洲位于地中海，距离巴塞罗那以南仅两小时路程，每年生产 1.2 亿公斤稻米，使其成为非洲大陆最重要的稻米种植区之一。然而，随着海水渗入这些淡水沼泽，盐分的上升阻碍了水稻的生产。与此同时，海水也杀死了贪婪的巨型苹果螺，这是一种以稻苗为食的外来害虫。最有希望的策略已经成为利用一个敌人来对抗另一个敌人。

paragraphs.sourceText: The battle is currently being waged on land, in greenhouses at the University of Barcelona. Scientists working under the banner “Project Neurice” are seeking varieties of rice that can withstand the increasing salinity without losing the absorbency that makes European rice ideal for traditional Spanish and Italian dishes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 目前，这场战斗正在陆地上、巴塞罗那大学的温室里进行。在“Project Neurice”的旗帜下工作的科学家们正在寻找能够承受不断增加的盐度而又不失去吸水性的稻米品种，这种吸水性使欧洲稻米成为传统西班牙和意大利菜肴的理想选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: “The project has two sides,” says Xavier Serrat, Neurice project manager and researcher at the University of Barcelona. “The short-term fight against the snail, and a mid- to long-term fight against climate change. But the snail has given the project greater urgency.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “该项目有两个方面，”巴塞罗那大学 Neurice 项目经理兼研究员 Xavier Serrat 说。 “短期是对抗蜗牛，中长期是对抗气候变化。但蜗牛让这个项目变得更加紧迫。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Originally from South America, the snails were accidentally introduced into the Ebro Delta by Global Aquatic Technologies, a company that raised the snails for fresh-water aquariums （水族馆）, but failed to prevent their escape. For now, the giant apple snail’s foothold in Europe is limited to the Ebro Delta. But the snail continues its march to new territory, says Serrat. “The question is not if it will reach other rice-growing areas of Europe, but when.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些蜗牛原产于南美洲，被全球水产技术公司（一家为淡水水族馆饲养蜗牛的公司）意外引入埃布罗三角洲，但未能阻止它们逃走。目前，巨型苹果螺在欧洲的立足点仅限于埃布罗三角洲。但塞拉特说，蜗牛仍在继续向新领域进军。 “问题不在于它是否会到达欧洲其他水稻种植区，而在于何时到达。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Over the next year and a half investigators will test the various strains of saline-tolerant rice they’ve concocted. In 2018, farmers will plant the varieties with the most promise in the Ebro Delta and Europe’s other two main rice-growing regions—along the Po in Italy, and France’s Rhône. A season in the field will help determine which, if any, of the varieties are ready for commercialization.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在接下来的一年半时间里，研究人员将测试他们炮制的各种耐盐水稻品种。 2018年，农民将在埃布罗三角洲和欧洲另外两个主要水稻种植区——意大利波河沿岸和法国罗讷河谷种植最有前景的品种。田间的一个季节将有助于确定哪些品种（如果有的话）已准备好商业化。

paragraphs.sourceText: As an EU-funded effort, the search for salt-tolerant varieties of rice is taking place in all three countries. Each team is crossbreeding a local European short-grain rice with a long-grain Asian variety that carries the salt-resistant gene. The scientists are breeding successive generations to arrive at varieties that incorporate salt tolerance but retain about 97 percent of the European rice genome （基因组）.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为欧盟资助的一项工作，这三个国家都在寻找耐盐水稻品种。每个团队都将当地的欧洲短粒水稻与携带耐盐基因的长粒亚洲品种进行杂交。科学家们正在培育连续几代的品种，以获得具有耐盐性但保留了约 97% 的欧洲水稻基因组（基因组）的品种。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 51 至 55 题基于以下段落

paragraphs.sourceText: Photography was once an expensive, laborious ordeal reserved for life’s greatest milestones. Now, the only apparent cost to taking infinite photos of something as common as a meal is the space on your hard drive and your dining companion’s patience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 摄影曾经是一种昂贵、费力的考验，是为人生最伟大的里程碑而保留的。现在，对像一顿饭这样常见的东西拍摄无限张照片的唯一明显成本是硬盘空间和用餐同伴的耐心。

paragraphs.sourceText: But is there another cost, a deeper cost, to documenting a life experience instead of simply enjoying it? “You hear that you shouldn’t take all these photos and interrupt the experience, and it’s bad for you, and we’re not living in the present moment,” says Kristin Diehl, associate professor of marketing at the University of Southern California Marshall School of Business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但是，记录生活经历而不是简单地享受它是否还有另一种成本，更深层次的成本？南加州大学马歇尔商学院营销学副教授克里斯汀·迪尔 (Kristin Diehl) 表示：“你听说不应该拍摄所有这些照片并中断体验，这对你不利，而且我们不活在当下。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Diehl and her fellow researchers wanted to find out if that was true, so they embarked on a series of nine experiments in the lab and in the field testing people’s enjoyment in the presence or absence of a camera. The results, published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, surprised them. Taking photos actually makes people enjoy what they’re doing more, not less.
paragraphs.translationZh: 迪尔和她的研究人员同事想知道这是否属实，因此他们在实验室和现场进行了一系列九项实验，测试人们在有或没有相机的情况下的享受程度。发表在《人格与社会心理学杂志》上的结果令他们感到惊讶。拍照实际上可以让人们更多地享受他们正在做的事情，而不是更少。

paragraphs.sourceText: “What we find is you actually look at the world slightly differently, because you’re looking for things you want to capture, that you may want to hang onto,” Diehl explains. “That gets people more engaged in the experience, and they tend to enjoy it more.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “我们发现，你对世界的看法实际上略有不同，因为你正在寻找你想要捕捉、想要抓住的东西，”迪尔解释道。 “这会让人们更加投入到体验中，而且他们往往会更享受它。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Take sightseeing. In one experiment, nearly 200 participants boarded a double-decker bus for a tour of Philadelphia. Both bus tours forbade the use of cell phones but one tour provided digital cameras and encouraged people to take photos.
paragraphs.translationZh: 去观光。在一项实验中，近 200 名参与者登上了一辆双层巴士游览费城。两次巴士之旅都禁止使用手机，但其中一次提供数码相机并鼓励人们拍照。

paragraphs.sourceText: The people who took photos enjoyed the experience significantly more, and said they were more engaged, than those who didn’t.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与不拍照的人相比，拍照的人明显更喜欢这种体验，并表示他们更加投入。

paragraphs.sourceText: Snapping a photo directs attention, which heightens the pleasure you get from whatever you’re looking at, Diehl says. It works for things as boring as archaeological（考古的）museums, where people were given eye-tracking glasses and instructed either to take photos or not. “People look longer at things they want to photograph,” Diehl says. They report liking the exhibits more, too.
paragraphs.translationZh: 迪尔说，拍照可以吸引注意力，从而增强你从所看到的事物中获得的乐趣。它适用于像考古博物馆这样无聊的地方，人们戴着眼动追踪眼镜，并被指示要么拍照，要么不拍照。 “人们会花更长时间观察他们想要拍摄的事物，”迪尔说。他们表示也更喜欢这些展品。

paragraphs.sourceText: To the relief of Instagrammers（Instagram 用户）everywhere, it can even make meals more enjoyable. When people were encouraged to take at least three photos while they ate lunch, they were more immersed in their meals than those who weren’t told to take photos.
paragraphs.translationZh: 让各地的 Instagrammers（Instagram 用户）松一口气的是，它甚至可以让用餐变得更加愉快。当鼓励人们在吃午餐时至少拍三张照片时，他们比那些不被告知拍照的人更能沉浸在食物中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Was it the satisfying click of the camera? The physical act of the snap? No, they found; just the act of planning to take a photo—and not actually taking it—had the same joy-boosting effect. “If you want to take mental photos, that works the same way,” Diehl says. “Thinking about what you would want to photograph also gets you more engaged.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 是令人满意的相机咔嗒声吗？快照的物理行为？不，他们发现；只是计划拍照而不是实际拍照的行为也具有同样的增加快乐的效果。 “如果你想拍摄心灵照片，也是同样的方法，”迪尔说。 “思考你想要拍摄什么也会让你更加投入。”
